canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_closure ∈ O_P^closure, where O_P^closure is the set of finite algebraic Wilson-loop constraint systems (G,N,model,d,S,W,E_trace,E_loop,P_pos) for finite-N compact matrix models or finite-N lattice gauge theories
canonical_goal.target_object: A finite-N trace-reduced Wilson-loop closure result o_closure=(G,N,model,d,S,W,E_trace,E_loop,P_pos): G is SU(N) or U(N) with finite N≥2; model is either a one-matrix integral or a hypercubic lattice gauge theory; d is the number of spacetime lattice directions when model is a lattice theory; S is either Z=∫DU exp((N/λ)(tr(U†)+tr(U))) for the one-matrix integral or S=−(N/λ)∑_p tr(U_p) for the Wilson plaquette lattice action with λ>0; W(C_1,...,C_m)=⟨∏_{i=1}^m Tr(∏_{l∈C_i}U_l)⟩ is the normalized multi-trace Wilson-loop expectation with Tr=(1/N)tr; E_trace is a finite-N trace-reduction system that rewrites generated products with too many traces into products with retained trace count; E_loop is the Schwinger-Dyson/Makeenko-Migdal equation system after applying E_trace; and P_pos is a set of positive-semidefinite matrices M with entries M_{ij}=⟨O_i†O_j⟩ or reflection-positive variants. The end-state is closure of E_loop over retained Wilson-loop expectation variables: U(N) lattice equations retain at most N traces, SU(N) lattice equations retain at most N−1 traces, SU(3) examples retain single- and double-trace variables, and SU(2) lattice and continuum equations retain only single-trace variables W(C)=⟨Tr∏_{l∈C}U_l⟩.
feasibility_constraints: For the lattice component, link variables obey U_{x,μ}∈G and U_{x+μ,−μ}=U_{x,μ}†; a plaquette variable U_p is the ordered product of four link variables around p; the Wilson action is S=−(N/λ)∑_p tr(U_p) with λ>0; and the partition function is Z=∫DU exp(−S) over the Haar measure of the link variables.

For the one-matrix component, U∈SU(N) or U∈U(N), λ>0, Z=∫DU exp((N/λ)(tr(U†)+tr(U))), and the retained observables are normalized traces Tr(U^k) and finite products of such traces after applying finite-N trace identities.

For arbitrary GL(N) matrices M_1,...,M_{N+1}, ε^{a_1...a_{N+1}}ε^{b_1...b_{N+1}}(M_1)_{a_1b_1}...(M_{N+1})_{a_{N+1}b_{N+1}}=0, and expansion of the two ε-tensors rewrites tr(M_1)...tr(M_{N+1}) as a finite linear combination of products containing at most N traces.

For SU(N) matrices U, the relation Det(U)=Det(U†)=1, written as 1=(1/N!)ε^{a_1...a_N}ε^{b_1...b_N}(U†)_{a_1b_1}...(U†)_{a_Nb_N}, permits the SU(N) trace-reduction used here: generated products of N traces are rewritten as finite linear combinations of products containing at most N−1 traces.

For SU(2), the explicit trace-reduction identity is tr(U)tr(V)=tr(UV)+tr(UV†) for every U,V∈SU(2); after inserting suitable backtracking identities in lattice contours, every generated double-trace Wilson-loop expectation is replaced by a sum of single-trace Wilson-loop expectations.

For SU(3), the explicit trace-reduction identity is tr(U)tr(V)tr(W)=−tr(WVU)−tr(UVW)+tr(U)tr(VW)+tr(UV)tr(W)+tr(UW)tr(V)+tr(U†V)tr(U†W)−tr(U†VU†W) for every U,V,W∈SU(3); hence generated triple-trace terms are rewritten using single- and double-trace terms.

The loop equations are produced by infinitesimal changes U_{x,μ}→(I+iϵ)U_{x,μ} and U†_{x,μ}→U†_{x,μ}(I−iϵ), with ϵ†=ϵ and tr(ϵ)=0 for SU(N); setting the integral of the full variation to zero yields linear equations among Wilson-loop expectations once the finite-N trace-reduction identities have been substituted.

Each positivity block has the form M⪰0, meaning α* M α≥0 for every complex coefficient vector α of compatible length; the entries are Wilson-loop expectations obtained from M_{ij}=⟨O_i†O_j⟩ or from the corresponding reflected Wilson-line inner product.

success_set.definition: Σ_P^closure={o_closure: all generated loop equations E_loop are expressible using only retained Wilson-loop expectation variables and all retained positivity matrices P_pos are positive semidefinite. For the SU(2) lattice Wilson action, membership includes the closed single-trace equation (1/λ)∑_{μ≠±ν}[W(σ^l_{νμ}∘C_{lν})−W(σ^l_{μν}∘C_{lν})]+(1/2)∑_{l'ν∼lν∈C}(−1)^{(1+ν·ν')/2}(W(C^{(1)}_{x,ν}∘C^{(2)}_{y,ν'})+(1/2)W(C))=0 for every retained oriented contour C and varied link l_ν, where σ^l_{νμ} is the oriented plaquette containing l with directions ν,μ, C∘C' is contour concatenation at the shared link or point, C^{(1)} and C^{(2)} are the two contour pieces produced by cutting C at the overlapping links, and the sum over l'ν∼lν includes l_ν itself. For the SU(2) continuum case, membership includes ∂_{x_μ}(δW(C_x)/δσ_{μν}(x))=(λ/2)∮_C dy_ν δ^{(d)}(x−y)[(1/2)W(C_x)+W(C^{(1)}_{xy}∘overline{C^{(2)}_{yx}})], where δ/δσ_{μν}(x) is an area derivative at x, overline denotes reversal of the ordered Wilson product, and the integral is over the contour C.}

robustness_scope.ambient_space: Finite-N compact matrix-model and lattice-gauge Wilson-loop systems whose observables are finite products of normalized traces and whose constraints are generated by infinitesimal integration-variable variations, finite-N trace identities, and positive-semidefinite Wilson-line inner products.
robustness_scope.indexing_set: {(G,N,model,d): G∈{SU(N),U(N)}, N∈ℤ, N≥2, model∈{one-matrix integral Z=∫DU exp((N/λ)(tr(U†)+tr(U))), hypercubic lattice Yang-Mills with S=−(N/λ)∑_p tr(U_p)}, and d∈ℤ,d≥1 when model is a lattice theory}

claimed_subfamily.definition: The claimed subfamily is formal closure, not uniform numerical tightness: U(N) finite-N loop equations close on at most N-trace Wilson variables, SU(N) finite-N loop equations close on at most (N−1)-trace Wilson variables, the SU(3) one-matrix and loop-equation examples close on single- and double-trace variables, and the SU(2) lattice and continuum loop equations close on single-trace variables.

robustness_scope.criterion: An indexed member (G,N,model,d) is in the claimed family exactly when every trace product generated by the loop-equation variation is rewritten by finite-N trace identities to a product containing at most N traces for U(N) or at most N−1 traces for SU(N), and after this substitution every retained equation is linear in retained Wilson-loop expectation variables and every retained positivity condition is a matrix inequality M⪰0 whose entries are retained Wilson-loop expectation variables.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_plaq ∈ O_P^plaq, where O_P^plaq is the set of finite collections of SU(2) plaquette intervals I_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)=[L_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P),U_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)] obtained from truncated Wilson-loop semidefinite feasible sets
canonical_goal.target_object: A collection of certified lower and upper intervals for the SU(2) lattice Yang-Mills plaquette average u_P=⟨Tr(U_P)⟩, where U_P is the ordered product of link variables around one plaquette and Tr=(1/2)tr. For each hierarchy level Λ, spacetime dimension d, and coupling λ>0, the output interval I_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)=[L_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P),U_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)] is obtained by minimizing and maximizing the same linear observable u_P over the same feasible set of retained single-trace Wilson-loop variables satisfying the SU(2) trace-reduced linear Makeenko-Migdal equations and Hermitian/reflection positive-semidefinite blocks. The lexicographic end-state first requires interval validity, L_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)≤u_P≤U_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P) for every feasible exact SU(2) lattice Wilson-loop solution projected to the retained variables; subject to validity, smaller interval width U_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)−L_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P) is preferred.
feasibility_constraints: The gauge group is SU(2); each link variable satisfies U_{x,μ}∈SU(2) and U_{x+μ,−μ}=U_{x,μ}†; the lattice action is S=−(2/λ)∑_p tr(U_p), equivalently β=8/λ under β=2N^2/λ with N=2; and λ>0.
The retained variables are single-trace Wilson-loop expectations W(C)=⟨Tr∏_{l∈C}U_l⟩ because tr(U)tr(V)=tr(UV)+tr(UV†) eliminates generated double-trace terms for SU(2).

The retained loop equations are the SU(2) single-trace lattice Makeenko-Migdal equations (1/λ)∑_{μ≠±ν}[W(σ^l_{νμ}∘C_{lν})−W(σ^l_{μν}∘C_{lν})]+(1/2)∑_{l'ν∼lν∈C}(−1)^{(1+ν·ν')/2}(W(C^{(1)}_{x,ν}∘C^{(2)}_{y,ν'})+(1/2)W(C))=0 for retained contours C and varied links l_ν.

The finite hierarchy assigns integer level 0 to the identity Wilson line, level 1 to the single plaquette Wilson line, and recursively assigns later levels by Schwinger-Dyson variations; if the retained Wilson-line basis has level at most Λ, then Wilson loops generated as inner products have maximum length L_max=8Λ.

The feasible set contains all retained x satisfying A_{Λ,d,λ}x=b_{Λ,d,λ} and M_{r,Λ,d,λ}(x)⪰0 for each retained Hermitian-conjugation or reflection-positivity block r, where each M_r(x) is affine in x.
The displayed high-resolution numerical case Λ=3 has L_max=8Λ=24, because the hierarchy rule defines L_max as eight times the Wilson-line level cutoff.

success_set.definition: Σ_P^plaq={o_plaq: for every included tuple (Λ,d,λ), L_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)=min_x u_P(x) and U_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)=max_x u_P(x) over the identical feasible set F_{Λ,d,λ}={x: A_{Λ,d,λ}x=b_{Λ,d,λ} and M_{r,Λ,d,λ}(x)⪰0 for all retained positivity blocks r}; L_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)≤U_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P); and the plotted plaquette band is the interval [L_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P),U_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)]. For the Λ=3 calculations the retained loop length is L_max=24 by L_max=8Λ, and the target observable is u_P=W(□)=⟨Tr(U_P)⟩.}

preference_ordering.definition: For two plaquette-bound outputs o and o', o⪰_P^plaq o' exactly when either every interval in o is valid and some interval in o' is invalid, or both outputs have valid intervals for the same indexed tuples and ∑_{(Λ,d,λ)}(U'_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)−L'_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)) ≥ ∑_{(Λ,d,λ)}(U_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)−L_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)); validity is ordered before tightness.

robustness_scope.ambient_space: SU(2) hypercubic lattice Yang-Mills plaquette-bound computations whose feasible sets are finite hierarchy truncations of the single-trace loop equations with positive-semidefinite Wilson-line inner-product constraints.
robustness_scope.indexing_set: {(d,Λ,λ): d∈{2,3,4}, Λ∈ℤ, Λ≥0, λ>0, retained loop length L_max=8Λ}

claimed_subfamily.definition: The claimed numerical subfamily consists of SU(2) plaquette intervals computed from the hierarchy-truncated convex feasible set in d=2, d=3, and d=4; the most detailed displayed finite-loop case uses Λ=3 and therefore L_max=24, and the d=3 and d=4 plotted bands are compared to Monte Carlo plaquette data across the displayed coupling ranges.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_string ∈ O_P^string, where O_P^string is the set of SU(2) finite-rectangle Creutz-ratio estimates a^2σ_{T,L,λ} derived from retained rectangular Wilson-loop expectations W(T,L)
canonical_goal.target_object: A set of SU(2) finite-loop string-tension estimates computed from retained rectangular Wilson-loop expectations. For rectangle sizes T,L with T≥2 and L≥2, define W(T,L)=⟨Tr(U_{T×L})⟩, where U_{T×L} is the ordered product of SU(2) link variables around a T-by-L lattice rectangle, and define the Creutz-type estimator a^2σ_{T,L,λ}=−log(W(T,L)W(T−1,L−1)/(W(T−1,L)W(T,L−1))). The end-state is not a certified infinite-area string tension limit; it is a qualitative estimate obtained by substituting retained finite-rectangle Wilson-loop values, with the implemented small-loop extraction using T=3 and L=2 so that a^2σ_{3,2,λ}=−log(W(3,2)W(2,1)/(W(2,2)W(3,1))).
feasibility_constraints: The gauge group is SU(2); link variables obey U_{x,μ}∈SU(2) and U_{x+μ,−μ}=U_{x,μ}†; the lattice action is S=−(2/λ)∑_p tr(U_p) with λ>0; retained variables are single-trace Wilson-loop expectations W(C)=⟨Tr∏_{l∈C}U_l⟩; the retained equations are the SU(2) trace-reduced linear Makeenko-Migdal equations; and the feasible set is F_{Λ,d,λ}={x:A_{Λ,d,λ}x=b_{Λ,d,λ} and M_{r,Λ,d,λ}(x)⪰0 for all retained Hermitian-conjugation or reflection-positivity blocks r}, where x contains the retained W(C) values and each M_r(x) is affine in x.
The rectangular Wilson-loop variables W(T,L), W(T−1,L−1), W(T−1,L), and W(T,L−1) must all be retained variables or computable from retained variables in F_{Λ,d,λ}.
The logarithm in a^2σ_{T,L,λ}=−log(W(T,L)W(T−1,L−1)/(W(T−1,L)W(T,L−1))) is defined only when W(T,L)W(T−1,L−1)/(W(T−1,L)W(T,L−1)) is positive.
For the small-loop extraction T=3,L=2, the required retained variables are W(3,2), W(2,1), W(2,2), and W(3,1), and the substituted estimator is a^2σ_{3,2,λ}=−log(W(3,2)W(2,1)/(W(2,2)W(3,1))).

success_set.definition: Σ_P^string={o_string: each included a^2σ_{T,L,λ} is computed by substituting retained SU(2) rectangular Wilson-loop expectations into a^2σ_{T,L,λ}=−log(W(T,L)W(T−1,L−1)/(W(T−1,L)W(T,L−1))), the four Wilson-loop values used in each logarithm are produced from the same hierarchy-truncated feasible-set computation, and the result is interpreted as a finite-rectangle Creutz estimate rather than as a proof of the T,L→∞ limit of the physical string tension.}

preference_ordering.definition: For two string-estimate outputs using the same retained rectangular loop variables, o⪰_P^string o' when o computes every stated Creutz expression from Wilson-loop values produced by a single internally consistent SU(2) bootstrap feasible set and o' omits at least one required retained rectangle or mixes rectangle values from different feasible-set computations; no total numerical accuracy ordering is claimed because the finite-rectangle estimator is presented as qualitative.

methodological_claim.target_object: The finite-N SU(2) bootstrap computations are convex semidefinite programs: after the identity tr(U)tr(V)=tr(UV)+tr(UV†) rewrites every generated double-trace term as single-trace terms, the retained Makeenko-Migdal equations are affine equations A(λ)x=b(λ) in the vector x of single-trace Wilson-loop expectations and the retained positivity constraints are affine matrix inequalities M_r(x)⪰0; therefore minimizing or maximizing any linear retained observable q^T x over the retained feasible set is a semidefinite optimization problem and does not require an auxiliary relaxation of quadratic large-N factorization variables.

source_span.verbatim: The SU(2) Makeenko-Migdal loop equations on the lattice are linear and closed exclusively on single-trace Wilson loops. ... The inherent linearity of the SU(2) loop equations renders the entire bootstrap procedure convex from the very beginning. ... min / max, subject to MM loop equations, HerMirrep ⪰ 0, RefMirrep ⪰ 0, ×3.

evidence_channels.formalisation: Let x=(W(C_1),...,W(C_k)) be the retained vector of SU(2) single-trace Wilson-loop expectations. Substitution of tr(U)tr(V)=tr(UV)+tr(UV†) turns every retained loop equation into A(λ)x=b(λ). Each retained Hermitian or reflection-positivity block has the affine form M_r(x)⪰0. Hence L(q)=min_x q^T x and U(q)=max_x q^T x subject to A(λ)x=b(λ) and M_r(x)⪰0 for all r are convex semidefinite optimization problems.

inference_basis: Aim spans in the abstract and main-results section explicitly combine a finite-N framework with a SU(2) application in d=2,3,4; this supports one formal closure goal plus two SU(2) output goals rather than one merged numerical goal.

Method artefacts define trace identities, trace-reduced loop equations, positivity constraints, symmetry reduction, and the hierarchy-truncated min/max semidefinite program, matching G1 and G2 exactly.

Evaluation artefacts split into plaquette upper/lower bands and separate string-tension plots from Creutz ratios; separating G2 and G3 avoids merging certified intervals with qualitative finite-rectangle estimates.

Prospect statements on quarks, baryons, matrix quantum mechanics, and larger N are future scope or hinted superfamilies because the operational numerical outputs are the SU(2) plaquette intervals and finite-rectangle string estimates.
implicit_goal.formalisation: The implicit best-fit hypothesis is an instrumental three-part goal: first, derive finite-N trace-reduced Wilson-loop closure systems with positive-semidefinite constraints for finite-N matrix/lattice gauge models; second, use the SU(2) single-trace convex feasible set to compute certified plaquette intervals [L_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P),U_{Λ,d,λ}(u_P)]; third, use retained rectangular Wilson-loop expectations to compute finite-rectangle Creutz estimates a^2σ_{T,L,λ}=−log(W(T,L)W(T−1,L−1)/(W(T−1,L)W(T,L−1))). The fit value is 0.20·1.0+0.30·1.0+0.30·1.0+0.20·0.96−0.05·0.315=0.97625.
